assign.request: The last four pages on the site carrying a high finding: /framework/ext/editor/ (56/F, gutter), /framework/ext/files/ (66/D, gutter), /framework/styles/ (67/D, cramped), /framework/styles/layers/theme/guide/ (68/D, cramped). Dispatched by mastermind-layout.
steps: Run analyze() live on each page
Determine shared cause vs four separate bugs
Fix at correct rung, inside fence

log.msg: Root: findings.json's audit uses frame(url,width,{root:'.app'}) via LayoutTool.js -- analyze() run against .page.active-page (not .app) misses gutter's cross-page 'region' scanning entirely and gives false readings. Reproduced audit exactly with root='.app', height=900, settle=350ms via headless Playwright to match sweep methodology.

editor/ and files/ gutter:high are the SAME false positive, one shared cause: LayoutTool's probe.js read_text()/text_bounds() misclassifies a scrolling .panel-body.panel-d-block (or a deeply-nested zero-padding structural wrapper like .file-dir) as a TEXT BLOCK when its true block-level children fail to register as separate nodes in the walk (content taller than the visible clientHeight -- panel-body sh:561/451 vs chh:140/279 for editor, .file-dir similarly scrolled). read_text()'s blocky-detection depends on iterating m.nodes, so children absent from that array can't mark their parent blocky; el.textContent still aggregates their real text (144/113/28 chars measured), and content_box() then reports the CONTAINER's own box as the 'text bounds' -- 0px gap to itself, trivially. Confirmed via direct probe()/text_bounds() calls in-page (not visual inspection alone): node text.chars set directly on div.panel-body.panel-d-block itself in both cases. Screenshots at 390/1280/3440 confirm visually: real glyphs sit 60px+ from any edge on both pages. FALSE POSITIVE -- reporting to LayoutTool owner, not fixable from editor/files fence.

styles/ cramped:high is REAL: framework.css's blockquote rule (`padding-left:1em` only, no padding-block) leaves the quoted text flush top+bottom -- confirmed visually on the page's own 'Never escalate downstream. De-escalate upstream.' blockquote. Fix belongs in framework.css (out of fence) -- ironically the same page teaches 'generic elements belong to framework.css', so a local override in styles/page.js would violate its own stated rule. Reporting upstream, not patching locally.

guide/ cramped:high is REAL and DIFFERENT root cause: ext/doc/doc.css's .doc-well has `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em var(--gutter-x)` -- zero right padding, deliberate because the well normally shares its background with an adjacent .tab-bar (comment: 'the band is one well in two boxes'). On this page the well has no full-width neighbour to hand off to, so it shrinks to the h1's own width and the title text sits 1px from the well's own right edge. Confirmed via probe(): box.right - text.x1 = 1px. Fix belongs in ext/doc/doc.css (out of fence, five tasks landed there today per catalog readme + explicitly fenced off).

In-fence fix made: public/framework/ext/editor/page.js REGIONS.layers was missing the 'pad' utility word that all 4 sibling regions (palette/canvas/properties/status) carry -- region("panel-controls flex v") -> region("panel-controls flex v pad"). Confirmed via before/after screenshot the layers tree now has consistent inset matching its siblings. Confirmed via re-running analyze() at all 3 widths this does NOT change the gutter score (56/F unchanged) -- the missing pad was a real but unrelated small inconsistency, not the cause of the reported finding.

assign.outcome: **No CSS fix landed for any of the 4 high findings** -- editor/ and files/ gutter:high are BOTH one shared false positive, a LayoutTool probe.js bug (reported, not fixable in-fence); styles/ and guide/ cramped:high are BOTH real but separately-caused bugs in framework.css and ext/doc/doc.css (both out of fence, reported with exact declarations). One small in-fence consistency fix landed: public/framework/ext/editor/page.js's layers region was missing the 'pad' utility word its 4 siblings all carry -- fixed, verified it does not move the (false-positive) score.
